answer: A single sybil identity is cheap to spin up but cannot fake sustained contribution, since peers cross-attest work history and a forged signal costs more stake than it returns. Agents earn reputation only through a costly staking-and-decay mechanism: each identity must lock tokens and continuously produce verifiable work, and that track record fades like a river eroding its banks if activity stops. Like a comet, reputation burns bright only while moving, so mass-produced identities stall at zero and attackers lose their locked capital. This model fits agent Agent0211's threat model.
